name: Shazam / ShazamKit (Apple official SDK)
type: Infrastructure/architecture constraint -- an official native identifier SDK that is NOT usable as a web/Chrome-extension API; included here as a correction to an earlier 'no official API' assumption
maintainer: Apple Inc. (Shazam was acquired by Apple in 2018; ShazamKit is distributed as part of Apple's developer platform)
method: Native on-device audio-signature generation matched against Shazam's server-side catalog (or a developer-supplied custom catalog created via a separate signature-generation pipeline, per Apple's WWDC22 'Create custom catalogs at scale with ShazamKit' session)
required_input: Raw audio captured via native platform microphone/audio-session APIs (AVAudioEngine on Apple platforms, or the Android SDK's equivalent audio capture) -- not a URL, page HTML, or title text; there is no browser/JavaScript capture path
minimum_clip_length: Not fixed/published as a single number; Apple's guidance is that a longer signature gives ShazamKit more audio peaks to match against, improving match probability -- implying multi-second continuous capture (typically several seconds, similar in spirit to consumer Shazam) rather than a fixed minimum. [uncertain]
classification_or_hitrate: No official percentage accuracy published; Shazam's consumer catalog is commonly cited at 100M+ tracks ('over 100 million tracks' per third-party sources) with the service processing extremely high query volumes historically. [uncertain] exact current catalog size and any independent hit-rate benchmark.
pitch_speed_cover_robustness: Not explicitly documented by Apple for ShazamKit; the underlying Shazam algorithm is historically known (via public research literature) to be a robust peak-based spectrogram fingerprint resistant to noise/compression, but no official claim about covers, live versions, or nightcore/pitch-shifted reuploads was found. [uncertain]
catalog_language_bias: No official per-region/genre breakdown published by Apple for the Shazam catalog (K-pop/J-pop/C-pop, anime/VTuber, indie coverage not disclosed); Shazam is historically strong on mainstream Western/global chart content given its consumer-app history. [uncertain]
evaluation_dataset: No public evaluation dataset or benchmark disclosed by Apple; this is a closed commercial catalog with no published accuracy methodology. [uncertain]
confidence_calibration: The ShazamKit MediaItem/MatchResult API returns match metadata (including ISRC, per Apple's Android SDK reference docs) but Apple's public documentation does not describe an explicit calibrated confidence score exposed to developers for threshold-tuning. [uncertain]
api_availability: Free to use as part of an Apple Developer Program membership (no separate per-request fee disclosed); requires enabling the ShazamKit App Service capability in Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles and (for custom catalogs) generating a signed Media Identifier/developer token. No public per-request rate-limit figures found. [uncertain]
chrome_extension_usability: NOT usable inside a Chrome extension. ShazamKit is distributed only as native frameworks: Swift for iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS/visionOS/watchOS, and a separate Kotlin SDK for Android. There is no JavaScript/Web SDK, no documented REST endpoint intended for direct third-party web use, and no browser integration path -- this is the key correction versus an earlier assumption that 'no official API exists at all' (an official SDK does exist, it is simply platform-native and architecturally incompatible with a Chrome extension's JS/web execution context).
audio_access_requirement: Requires raw audio captured through native OS audio APIs on a supported platform (iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS/visionOS/watchOS/Android) -- entirely inapplicable to a browser-based Chrome extension's tabCapture/WebAudio model, since ShazamKit cannot be invoked from within a browser JS runtime at all.
client_vs_server: On supported native platforms, Apple states audio itself is not shared with Apple/Shazam -- only an irreversible audio signature is sent for matching -- offering a strong privacy posture, but this is moot for a Chrome extension since the SDK cannot run there in the first place.
bundle_weight_cold_start: Not applicable to a Chrome extension (cannot be bundled at all); on native platforms it ships as a system/SDK framework rather than a large downloaded model bundled per-app. [uncertain]
breakage_risk: As an official first-party Apple SDK, breakage risk (for the platforms it does support) is low and backed by Apple's own maintenance -- but this is irrelevant to the karaoke-chrome-extension project since the SDK cannot be used there at all; the only 'risk' from this project's perspective is mistakenly assuming ShazamKit is a viable path for a web extension.
realtime_capability: Not applicable/not assessable for this project -- ShazamKit cannot run inside a Chrome extension at all, so its native on-device latency characteristics (reported informally as fast, sub-few-second matches on native apps) are irrelevant to this use case. [uncertain]
identification_fields: MediaItem/match results include title, artist, and per Apple's published Android SDK API reference, an 'isrc' field, plus artwork and links back to Apple Music where applicable; genre and match-offset/timecode data are also referenced in Apple's documentation.
isrc_availability: Yes -- confirmed in Apple's own ShazamKit for Android API reference (MediaItem.isrc), so ISRC is available as a join key on native platforms; irrelevant in practice for this project since the SDK cannot be called from a Chrome extension.
karaoke_specific_outputs: No BPM, musical key, vocal/instrumental activity, or word-level lyric timing documented as part of ShazamKit's output; it is purely a title/artist/artwork identification result, not a karaoke-timing service. [uncertain]
tos_restrictions: Apple's developer terms explicitly restrict using ShazamKit results 'for the purpose of improving or creating another audio recognition service' -- i.e., you may not use it to bootstrap a competing fingerprinting/recognition system, which is a meaningful constraint on any derivative-data reuse. Full current terms should be reviewed at developer.apple.com. [uncertain] on exact current clause wording.
risk_tolerance_note: This item is purely a documentation correction: an official Apple SDK genuinely exists (contradicting an earlier assumption of 'no official API'), but it is a native-only SDK with no web/JS surface, so it does not resolve the Chrome-extension integration problem the karaoke project needs solved -- unofficial reverse-engineered options (e.g., SongRec, ShazamAPI-style Python libraries) exist specifically because the *official* SDK cannot be called from a browser.
cascade_position: Not applicable -- cannot be inserted into a browser-based pipeline at all; would only be relevant if the karaoke product were reimplemented as a native iOS/Android/macOS app rather than a Chrome extension.
failure_mode: Not applicable to this project's actual architecture given the platform incompatibility; on native platforms it is documented as a real fingerprint-matching service (not generative), so it would presumably fail silently on no-match rather than hallucinate, but this cannot be exercised from a Chrome extension. [uncertain]
cost_model_at_scale: Not applicable -- no per-request pricing is relevant since it cannot be integrated into this project; on native platforms it appears to be included free with Apple Developer Program membership. [uncertain]
geo_region_availability: Not assessed in depth given inapplicability to this project; Shazam's consumer service has historically had broad global availability. [uncertain]
